title: Add shadow association and claim-evidence question families
summary: Implement a small original family catalogue for ambiguous observation association and claim-relative evidence interpretation. The family produces shadow judgments over frozen candidate packets; it must preserve uncertain associations and cannot change identity or provenance merely because text is similar.
in_scope: Support, contradiction, qualification and asserted-versus-established evidence
out_of_scope: Automatic merges or confirmed speaker identity
Replacing deterministic exact identifiers with model scores
implementation: Define a fixed outcome set for each bounded candidate comparison with scope and identifiers resolved before semantic evaluation.
Define separate claim-relative predicates for support, contradiction and qualification, allowing compatible dimensions to coexist.
Bind each result to claim, candidate, packet, occurrence lineage and question revision, preserving the original observations.
Emit proposed associations and unresolved reasons for the core association policy; do not write accepted merges directly.
Add synthetic and labeled episode cases distinguishing shared topics, the same continuing matter, a repeated occurrence and independent corroboration.

acceptance.criterion: Topic similarity cannot automatically establish same matter, same occurrence or shared person identity.
acceptance.verification: Evaluate fixtures with identical wording across different tasks, executions and people and inspect proposed relations.

acceptance.criterion: A source assertion is distinguished from evidence that the asserted event occurred.
acceptance.verification: Compare planned funding with an authoritative award document under the same claim.

acceptance.criterion: Support and qualification can coexist without an invalid exclusive-choice collapse.
acceptance.verification: Use a passing unit test that supports one behavior but leaves integration verification unresolved.

tests: Two notices at one location have different project identifiers.
A model summary inherits its source lineage.
An ambiguous alias stays unresolved rather than becoming enrollment.
risks: Premature merges destroy the continuity that matters are meant to preserve.
A corroboration classifier cannot prove source independence.

reuse.application: Adapt novelty, contradiction, explicit-update and relevance distinctions using original Matter questions.

sources: jevinmatter — procedural evidence is a soft contextual example
